title: Module Overview: The 43-Year Journey to Condition (Ψ)
content: The module header presents a historical table spanning 1957-2006: Lewy's counterexample (1957) destroyed the assumption that smooth linear PDEs always have local solutions; Hörmander (1960) gave a necessary condition; Nirenberg-Treves (1963) conjectured condition (Ψ) as the precise characterization; Beals-Fefferman (1973) proved the stronger condition (P) suffices; and Dencker (2006) completed the conjecture. Three axioms remain: `IsLocallySolvable` (distribution theory gap), `hormander_necessity` (microlocal analysis), and `dencker_sufficiency` (Dencker's deep proof).
mathContext: The local solvability problem asks: given a smooth linear PDE $Pu = f$, when does a distribution solution $u \in \mathcal{D}'$ exist near every point $x_0$ for every smooth $f$? The principal symbol $p_m(x, \xi)$ encodes the leading-order behavior. Condition (Ψ): $\mathrm{Im}(p_m)$ cannot change sign from $-$ to $+$ along oriented bicharacteristics of $\mathrm{Re}(p_m)$. This is both necessary (Hörmander 1960) and sufficient (Dencker 2006) for principal-type operators.

title: LinearPDO and principalSymbol: Multi-Index Formalism
content: The multi-index representation is the algebraically clean way to encode differential operators in Lean: a `Fin n → ℕ` encodes the exponent tuple $(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_n)$, and the coefficient map `coeff : MultiIndex n → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ` compactly packages all the variable-coefficient data. The `order_bound` field enforces the crucial constraint that $P$ has finite order. The `principalSymbol` filters to `MultiIndex.order α = m` via an `if-then-else` inside `Finset.univ.sum`, extracting the homogeneous part and casting real $\xi$ components to complex.
mathContext: A linear PDO of order $m$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $P = \sum_{|\alpha| \leq m} a_\alpha(x) D^\alpha$ where $D^\alpha = \partial^{|\alpha|}/\partial x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots \partial x_n^{\alpha_n}$. The principal symbol $p_m(x, \xi) = \sum_{|\alpha| = m} a_\alpha(x) \xi^\alpha$ lives on the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{R}^n \cong \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n$ and determines all qualitative properties: ellipticity ($p_m \neq 0$ for $\xi \neq 0$), hyperbolicity (real $p_m$ with specified cone structure), and local solvability (condition (Ψ)).

title: IsLocallySolvable and IsPrincipalType: Two Missing Ingredients
content: `IsLocallySolvable` is axiomatized because Schwartz distributions $\mathcal{D}'$ (the dual of test functions $C_c^\infty$) are not yet in Mathlib. Rather than embedding a long distribution theory digression, the `axiom` pattern explicitly names the gap. `IsPrincipalType P` is a concrete `def`: for every $(x_0, \xi_0)$ with $p_m(x_0, \xi_0) = 0$ and $\xi_0 \neq 0$, the symbol has a nonzero partial derivative in some $\xi$-direction. This ensures the bicharacteristic flow is non-degenerate.
mathContext:
Local solvability at $x_0$: for every $f \in C^\infty$ near $x_0$, $\exists u \in \mathcal{D}'$ with $Pu = f$ in some neighborhood. Principal type: $p_m(x_0, \xi_0) = 0, \xi_0 
eq 0 \Rightarrow 
abla_\xi p_m(x_0, \xi_0) 
eq 0$. Principal type excludes operators like $P = \partial_x^2$ (symbol $\xi_1^2$ vanishes to second order at $\xi_1 = 0$) and ensures that the bicharacteristic curves of $\mathrm{Re}(p_m)$ are smooth non-degenerate curves in $T^*\mathbb{R}^n$.

title: BicharacteristicCurve and imSymbolAlongCurve: Symplectic Geometry in Lean
content: Encoding bicharacteristics as a `structure` rather than an `axiom` is a key design choice: it enables Lean to construct concrete bicharacteristic objects and reason about them in proved theorems (like `elliptic_satisfies_psi`). The omission of the Hamilton flow makes `ConditionPsi` stronger than the classical definition (more curves to check), so the deep axioms remain conservative — a deliberate over-approximation that preserves soundness. The bridge lemma `imSymbolAlongCurve_eq` proves that `imSymbolAlongCurve γ t` is indeed $\mathrm{Im}(p_m(x(t), \xi(t)))$.
mathContext:
A bicharacteristic curve of $\mathrm{Re}(p_m)$ is a curve $\gamma(t) = (x(t), \xi(t))$ in $T^*\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying: (1) $p_m(x(t), \xi(t)) = 0$ and (2) $\xi(t) 
eq 0$. In the full theory, $\gamma$ also follows the Hamilton flow $\dot{x} = 
abla_\xi \mathrm{Re}(p_m)$, $\dot{\xi} = -
abla_x \mathrm{Re}(p_m)$ — these are Hamilton's equations with Hamiltonian $H = \mathrm{Re}(p_m)$ and symplectic form $\omega = d\xi \wedge dx$ on $T^*\mathbb{R}^n$. The Hamilton flow condition is omitted here pending Mathlib ODE infrastructure.
prerequisites: Lean 4 structures with hypotheses as fields

title: Condition (Ψ): The Asymmetric Sign Condition
content: This sign condition — proposed by Nirenberg and Treves in 1963 and proved necessary and sufficient by Dencker in 2006 — is the precise obstruction to local solvability. The asymmetry ($- \to +$ is forbidden, but $+ \to -$ is allowed) reflects the oriented structure of the bicharacteristic flow. The Lean encoding as `¬(imSymbolAlongCurve γ t₂ > 0)` directly captures the forbidden $+$ arrival. The condition is vacuously true when no bicharacteristic curves exist (elliptic case).
mathContext: Condition (Ψ): $\forall$ bicharacteristic curve $\gamma$, $\forall t_1 < t_2$: $\mathrm{Im}(p_m(\gamma(t_1))) < 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Im}(p_m(\gamma(t_2))) \leq 0$. Equivalently, there is no $t_1 < t_2$ with $\mathrm{Im}(p_m) < 0$ at $t_1$ and $\mathrm{Im}(p_m) > 0$ at $t_2$. Lewy's example has $p_m = \xi_1 + iz\xi_3$ (for $n=3$, $m=1$), and $\mathrm{Im}(p_m) = z\xi_3$ changes sign along the bicharacteristics of $\mathrm{Re}(p_m) = \xi_1$, explaining its non-solvability.

title: hormander_necessity and dencker_sufficiency: The Two Halves of the Theorem
content: The two axioms represent fundamentally different levels of mathematical difficulty. `hormander_necessity` (Hörmander 1960): if $P$ is locally solvable and principal type, then condition (Ψ) holds. The proof uses a microlocal contradiction argument — if (Ψ) fails, a specific approximate solution construction shows $Pu = f$ has no distribution solution near the sign-change point. `dencker_sufficiency` (Dencker 2006): if (Ψ) holds, then $P$ is locally solvable. This is exponentially harder — it requires second microlocalization and a delicate energy estimate showing that (Ψ) prevents the loss of derivatives that would block solvability.
mathContext: Hörmander necessity: uses the fact that if $\mathrm{Im}(p_m)$ changes sign from $-$ to $+$ at some time $t_0$, one can construct a sequence of approximate solutions $u_k$ with $\|Pu_k\|_{H^s} \to 0$ but $\|u_k\|_{H^{s-m+1}}$ bounded below, contradicting a priori estimates for local solvability. Dencker sufficiency: uses a pseudodifferential operator calculus ($L^2$ Sobolev estimates, symbol classes $S^m_{\rho,\delta}$) and the geometrically subtle construction of a microlocal energy density that is non-increasing along bicharacteristics when (Ψ) holds.

title: nirenberg_treves_characterization: 43 Years of Mathematics in Four Lines
content: The proof is four lines of Lean because the deep mathematical content is captured by the two axioms `hormander_necessity` and `dencker_sufficiency`. This is the honest structure of the formalization: the logical skeleton of the equivalence is checked mechanically, while the two halves — each representing decades of hard analysis — are explicitly named as assumptions awaiting full formalization. The iff construction `⟨forward, backward⟩` is standard Lean for biconditionals.
mathContext: The theorem `IsLocallySolvable P x₀ ↔ ConditionPsi P` is proved as `⟨fun h => hormander_necessity P hpt x₀ h, fun h => dencker_sufficiency P hpt h x₀⟩`. Note the argument order differs: necessity takes the solvability proof $h$ and produces (Ψ), while sufficiency takes the (Ψ) proof $h$ and the point $x_0$ separately. The hypothesis `hpt : IsPrincipalType P` threads through both directions — without it, neither direction holds.

title: Elliptic Special Case: Three Theorems, One Design Principle
content: `real_symbol_satisfies_psi`: if $\mathrm{Im}(p_m) = 0$ everywhere, then (Ψ) holds because its hypothesis $\mathrm{Im}(p_m(\gamma(t_1))) < 0$ is never satisfied (it equals 0 by assumption), so the conclusion is vacuously true. `elliptic_satisfies_psi`: no bicharacteristic curve can exist for an elliptic $P$ (it would require $p_m = 0$ and $\xi \neq 0$ simultaneously), so the universal quantifier in (Ψ) has empty domain. `elliptic_locally_solvable` chains: elliptic ⟹ (Ψ) via `elliptic_satisfies_psi` ⟹ solvable via `dencker_sufficiency`.
mathContext: `elliptic_satisfies_psi` proof: `exact absurd (γ.symbol_vanishes 0) (hell (γ.x 0) (γ.ξ 0) (γ.ξ_ne_zero 0))`. The `absurd` combinator takes `h : A` and `h' : ¬A` and produces any type. Here $A$ = `principalSymbol P (γ.x 0) (γ.ξ 0) = 0` (from `γ.symbol_vanishes 0`) and $\neg A$ = `principalSymbol P (γ.x 0) (γ.ξ 0) ≠ 0` (from `hell (γ.x 0) (γ.ξ 0) (γ.ξ_ne_zero 0)`). The `real_symbol_satisfies_psi` proof uses `linarith` to derive $0 < 0$ from `hreal` (giving $= 0$) and `hneg` (giving $< 0$).
